You know that moment when the light hits the kitchen table just right, and suddenly you notice the grain of the wood, the little scars and stains, the way it has quietly held a thousand cups of coffee and a hundred dinners and someone’s homework and someone’s tears? It was always there. But for a second, you really see it. That’s the kind of thing I want to write about: the way attention turns ordinary things into almost sacred things.

We spend so much time rushing toward the next thing—the next notification, the next goal, the next version of ourselves we think we should be. Meanwhile, the world is doing its slow, spectacular thing right under our noses. Moss is spreading on the north side of a tree. A spider is repairing its web with impossible precision. The refrigerator hums its one steady note, like a monk chanting. And none of it asks anything of us except that we show up.

Sometimes I think we are all just trying to be witnessed. Not in a big, dramatic way, but in the quiet way that sunlight witnesses a leaf. That’s what writing is, maybe: an act of attention, a decision to say, “This mattered. I saw it. I’m trying to keep it.”

And it’s okay if it’s messy. It’s okay if the thoughts wander like a creek that doesn’t care where it’s going. Because wandering is how we find the mossy stones, the cool shadows, the tiny worlds we would have missed on a straight road. So here I am, wandering on purpose, just to see what becomes visible.

What I’m learning is that joy isn’t always loud. It’s often just the relief of being present, even briefly, in a body, in a room, in a universe that is both terrifying and beautiful. It’s the warmth of a mug in your hands. It’s the sound of rain that never quite makes up its mind. It’s the absurd, tender fact that you and I are both here, right now, existing at the same time in this vast and improbable cosmos.

So thank you for listening to me wander. Go find the grain of your own table. Look at the thing you’ve passed a thousand times. Let it touch you. Then come back and tell someone about it, if you want. Or don’t. The moment is enough.

That’s the whole secret, I think. The moment is enough.
